title: Film Festivals
objective: After this level you can explain what festivals like Venice and Cannes do and how they carry films from one country to the world.
summary: Venice (1932) is the oldest film festival; Cannes, planned for 1939, opened in 1946. Their prizes and markets carry films across borders.

cards.headline: A film from Japan wins in Italy, and the world starts watching.
cards.body: Remember Rashomon (Level 63)? Its Golden Lion at Venice in 1951 opened Western markets to Japanese films. That's a festival's superpower: one screening can carry a film across borders. How do festivals pull it off?

cards.headline: The oldest and its rival
cards.body: The Venice Film Festival, founded in 1932 as part of the Venice Biennale, is the world's oldest film festival; its top prize is the Golden Lion. France's Philippe Erlanger imagined a rival, a festival free of political pressure. Cannes was due to open on 1 September 1939, the day Germany invaded Poland. It finally opened in 1946.

cards.headline: Prizes and a marketplace
cards.body: Festivals do two jobs. First, prizes: Cannes gave its first Palme d'Or in 1955, and its awards lifted Pather Panchali in 1956 and Truffaut in 1959. Second, business: Cannes became a marketplace where producers and distributors view films and sign contracts, and its film market, the Marché du Film, became official in 1959. The prize gets a film noticed; the contract gets it shown.

cards.headline: A hall named for the first paying crowd
cards.body: At Cannes, the festival's ceremonies fill the main auditorium of the Palais des Festivals, which bears the name of cinema pioneer Louis Lumière. In 1895 he and his brother held a Paris showing that Britannica calls the beginning of cinema history. Every year, new films meet their first big crowds under his name.

cards.headline: Festivals: attended
learned: Venice, 1932: the oldest; top prize the Golden Lion
Prizes spotlight films; markets sell them
Cannes's main hall honors Louis Lumière

questions.prompt: The world's oldest film festival is _____.

options.label: Berlin
options.rationale: Venice, founded in 1932, is the oldest.

options.label: the Marché du Film
options.rationale: That's the Cannes film market, not a festival.

questions.explanation: Venice, founded in 1932 as part of the Venice Biennale, is the world's oldest film festival.

questions.prompt: Put these festival moments in order, from earliest to latest.
questions.explanation: The Venice Film Festival was founded in 1932. Cannes was due to open in 1939, the day Germany invaded Poland. Cannes gave its first Palme d'Or in 1955, lifted Pather Panchali in 1956, and made the Marché du Film official in 1959.

questions.prompt: Cannes's main hall is named for Louis Lumière. What did the Lumières do on December 28, 1895?

options.label: Won the first prize at a film festival
Opened the first Kinetoscope parlor
options.rationale: That was in New York, with Edison's machines.

options.label: Projected films for a paying public in Paris
Shot the first film with fully synchronized sound

questions.explanation: December 28, 1895 was the Lumières' commercial premiere: projected films for a paying audience.
